participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, runs the meeting)
summary: Opens as the Primal Instinct sales team meeting: wins, then week-to-date projections. Ben Byrne reports zero units and is holding a target of three; Kim Forbes-Sobers reports three sets and a 100% show rate; kyla louie reports five sets and no units and has her weekly target cut from 17 to 12 because she is off Friday. Chris Klevan attributes the show rate to application changes and to an automated pre-call messaging bot. At 00:12:54 the setters are dismissed and the remaining fifty minutes are a one-to-one coaching session between Chris Klevan and Ben Byrne on why Ben's prospects are not seeing $6,000 of value. Chris walks through his own sequence — current situation, past attempts, future pacing, timing, commitment, pre-pitch, pitch — and teaches an identity-based 'pre-pitch' that validates the prospect as the kind of person who succeeds, before the programme is described. The session ends on a long tangent about David Hawkins, consciousness and God.
notable: SETTER MAPPING CONFIRMED — Kim Forbes-Sobers (KFS) and kyla louie (KL) are both present as setters on the Primal Instinct team, alongside closers Ben Byrne and Andrew Musial under manager Chris Klevan. This is direct corroboration for the KFS and KL title suffixes used across the corpus.

The sales manager explicitly directs a closer away from the Consequence Frame, which is Phase 5 of the company playbook and carries a 20% weight: 'I don't really love that stuff... I don't like consequence with pride very much... it's just not how I sell.' Ben accepts: 'Yeah, I mean, I'll just try it that way, more empowering.'

Chris teaches a different process from the documented playbook — current situation, past attempts, future, timing, commitment, pre-pitch, pitch — including a 'pre-pitch' phase that does not exist in the playbook at all, and for which he says he has recorded a separate training.

The pre-pitch is taught as generic identity validation that works regardless of the individual: 'it's almost like I'm qualifying that they're the right fit. Like they're the type of person that we get the best results for no matter who they are' and 'You can just use that for anybody... that's why it works so well is because so many people feel that way about themselves.'

Stated close policy: 'The only reason people don't move forward is because they literally don't have the money or I have to take a deposit. They have to talk to their spouse.' Confirms deposits are taken in practice.

Ben describes an open deal where the prospect's objection is an active divorce: 'his objection was that he's going through a divorce, and he has to talk to his lawyer to figure out the money situation, but that's going to happen next week, and he said he wants to do the one-on-one coaching.'
Ben reports a live price anchor well below the offer: 'I had a guy... Tuesday, he's like, oh, I don't want to spend any more than $2,000, or $3,000, I think was his max.'

An automated bot messages booked prospects on a schedule before the call: 'every like three hours before a call now, it starts to send them another message'. No mention of whether prospects are told the messages are automated.

Commission structure surprise: Ben learns on this call that closers earn commission on Primal University sales — 'Yeah, you would definitely get comms for that' / 'Didn't even know that was an option.'

Ben uses the word manipulate for his own understanding of the method: 'it's less empowering, I guess, for you to, like, get them to the point mentally, whether you have to manipulate them in to do that or whatever, where it's like, okay, this is something you need to do.'
Recording disclosure was made at the top of the call: 'This meeting is being recorded.'

Product structure: Primal University is the lower-tier community product and Kettlebell Body is the paid upgrade; Chris proposes seeding Primal University with Kettlebell Body wins so members 'might need to upgrade'.
